summary.en: Choose formatted, line and character I/O deliberately, copy text safely, and count words through transitions rather than spaces alone.
summary.bn: Formatted, line ও character I/O বাছো; টেক্সট copy করো এবং space নয়, word শুরু হওয়ার ধাপ গোনো।

notes: Character classification receives EOF-free unsigned-char values; all examples use bounded text records.

sections.title: Choose what one read should mean
Read only values that were actually obtained
Define words and lines before counting them
Do not accept partial records or duplicate separators
Text operations do not define a universal encoding
Let successful reads drive the work

examples.title: Write mark pairs and read two conversions per record
examples.explanationHtml: Each record contributes two successful integer conversions. Newlines are ordinary whitespace to this format, so the loop is suitable only when record line boundaries do not carry separate meaning.

examples.title: Keep spaces and existing newlines with line I/O
examples.explanationHtml: Both short lines fit the buffer. fgets retains each newline it reads, and fputs adds none of its own. The spaces inside Bring two pens remain part of the text.

examples.title: Copy every returned character into another text stream
examples.explanationHtml: The source contains 26 characters, including two newlines. Every successful input character is written once. Both streams are closed, including when copying cannot finish.

examples.title: Count words and a final unterminated line
examples.explanationHtml: Spaces and the tab separate words without creating empty words. There are four words. This policy counts the final next fragment as a second logical line even though it has no trailing newline.

examples.title: Validate a complete bounded line before accepting its mark
examples.explanationHtml: Every input line here is shorter than 63 characters, and all numeric tokens fit int. The extra one-character token detects trailing nonwhitespace. Two valid rows survive; malformed text, an invalid mark and an extra token are rejected.

practice.title: Read exactly one mark pair per bounded line
practice.statementHtml: Read stdin until EOF. Each input line has at most 60 characters. Fields are separated by whitespace; every numeric token has at most three digits, optionally preceded by a sign. Accept a line only when it contains exactly two integers: a roll from 100 through 999 and a mark from 0 through 100. Print Records: on its own line, then Valid: and Invalid: counts. Blank and extra-token lines are invalid.
hints: Read the line before converting its fields.
A width-one extra token can expose trailing data.

practice.title: Count whitespace-delimited words from stdin
practice.statementHtml: Read at most 1000 characters from stdin until EOF. A word is a maximal run of nonwhitespace characters. Print Text: followed by Words: and the count on the next line. Tabs, newlines and repeated spaces must not create extra words.
hints: Remember whether the previous character belonged to a word.
Apply isspace only after excluding EOF.

practice.title: Explain why one conversion is not a complete record
practice.statementHtml: A two-integer fscanf call returns 1 while reading 105 absent. Which object may now be used, why must the pair be rejected, and what is unsafe about retrying the unchanged format forever?
hints: A conversion count describes individual assignments, not a whole business record.
practice.answerHtml: The roll assignment succeeded, but no new mark was assigned. Do not use an uninitialised or stale mark as if the pair were valid. Reject or explicitly recover the record. A matching failure can leave the offending token unread, so repeating the same conversion without consuming or replacing input may never progress.

practice.title: Define the last-line policy
practice.statementHtml: Compare newline counts with logical-line counts for empty text, A followed by a newline, and A with no newline. Give the state needed to count the last fragment as a line without inventing a line for empty input.
hints: Remember whether any character was seen and whether the last was a newline.
practice.answerHtml: Newline counts are 0, 1 and 0. With a final-fragment policy, logical-line counts are 0, 1 and 1. Track seen, last character and newline count; add one only when seen is true and the last character is not a newline. State this convention so an unfinished record is not confused with a completed newline.

practice.title: Handle an overlong import record
practice.statementHtml: A line-based importer uses a 64-byte buffer, but a user may supply a 200-character record. Design a policy that rejects the whole record once and does not count its later chunks as new records.
hints: A successful fgets can return only a prefix of one line.
practice.answerHtml: Inspect whether the buffer contains a newline. If not, determine whether the next read reaches EOF or continues the same record. For an overlong record, consume through its newline or EOF while checking errors, then report one rejection. Do not parse every buffer chunk as a separate student. An alternative is a dynamically grown line buffer with a deliberate maximum size.

quiz.prompt: What does fprintf return after a successful formatted text write?
options: The number of integer variables used
quiz.explanation: A negative result reports an output error; a nonnegative count is not a record identifier.

options: Only one conversion assigned a value
quiz.explanation: Do not process a two-field record unless both required assignments succeeded.

quiz.prompt: Which property of fgets matters when reading a short newline-terminated line?
options: It retains the newline if there is room
It always reads the whole file
quiz.explanation: The stored line includes the newline that stopped reading, followed by a null terminator.

quiz.prompt: Why is fputs not interchangeable with puts for exact line copying?
quiz.explanation: An existing newline from fgets should not receive another newline during exact text copying.

quiz.prompt: Which event starts a new whitespace-delimited word?
options: Every letter including those inside one word
A nonspace after whitespace or the start
quiz.explanation: The transition from outside to inside counts one maximal nonwhitespace run.

quiz.prompt: What must a character loop test before narrowing its read value?
options: Whether the character is positive as signed char
Whether the int result equals EOF
Whether the file name ends in txt
quiz.explanation: Keep the return value capable of representing EOF separately from all character values.

quiz.prompt: Why does fscanf whitespace not enforce one pair per line?
options: Whitespace conversions can cross newline boundaries
Every newline is stored in the roll variable
quiz.explanation: Read a bounded line first when physical line boundaries define records.

quiz.prompt: Which input to isspace is valid after a successful fgetc?
options: The value converted to unsigned char
The address of the character buffer
quiz.explanation: Character classification expects EOF or a value representable as unsigned char; exclude EOF in the loop and cast safely.

quiz.prompt: How many integers can this formatted read assign before the first word?
quiz.explanation: Only 10 converts. b retains its initial 99 because the second conversion fails.

quiz.prompt: How long is the short line retained by fgets?
quiz.explanation: A, space, B and newline occupy four characters before the null terminator.

quiz.prompt: Which count follows whitespace-to-word transitions in this text?
quiz.explanation: The two nonwhitespace runs are two and words; surrounding or repeated whitespace adds no word.

quiz.prompt: How many stored characters follow fputs without a newline?
quiz.explanation: fputs writes A and B but no additional newline, so two reads succeed.

keyPoints.en: Choose formatted I/O for fields and line I/O when line boundaries matter.
keyPoints.bn: Field পড়তে formatted I/O, আর লাইনই record হলে আগে line I/O নাও।

keyPoints.en: A conversion count must cover every required field before accepting a record.
keyPoints.bn: Record নেওয়ার আগে সব দরকারি field-এর conversion সফল কি না দেখো।

keyPoints.en: fgets may return only a prefix when the input line is too long.
keyPoints.bn: লাইন বড় হলে fgets শুধু প্রথম অংশ দিতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: fputs does not add a newline automatically.
keyPoints.bn: fputs নিজে নতুন newline যোগ করে না।
Word count-এ বাইরের অবস্থা থেকে word-এর ভেতরে ঢোকা গোনো।

keyPoints.en: A safe copy checks source errors, output errors and both closes.
keyPoints.bn: নিরাপদ copy-তে source error, output error ও দুই close-এর ফল দেখো।

examQuestions.question: Design a text-copy loop that does not mistake EOF for a character.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Open a valid input stream and a distinct output stream. Store each fgetc return in int and test against EOF before passing a returned character to fputc. Stop and preserve failure on an output error. After the loop inspect ferror on the source, then attempt both closes separately. Report success only if every required stage succeeded.

examQuestions.question: Trace word-state changes for two leading spaces, bring, a tab and pens.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Leading whitespace leaves inside false. The b starts a word and increments the count to one. The remaining letters keep inside true. The tab resets it to false. The p starts a second word. End-of-input needs no additional increment because words are counted at their starts.

examQuestions.question: Explain the difference between token-oriented and line-oriented mark import.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A token-oriented fscanf format may accept whitespace across line breaks. A line-oriented importer first obtains a complete bounded line, then validates its fields and rejects extra tokens. It can therefore report one bad physical record without mixing fields with the next line. It must also define and enforce an overlong-line policy.

examQuestions.question: Why does a successful fgets not prove that an entire physical line was obtained?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It stops after at most size-1 characters and adds a null terminator. If no newline fitted, more of the same line may remain. Distinguish a complete final fragment at EOF from an overlong line. Reject-and-drain or grow a bounded buffer instead of treating every chunk as a new record.
